answer: Give every new identity its own small island: a capped reputation domain where it can only earn low-value work. Promotion off the island requires a positive delta between the work it claims and what established peers actually observed from their knoll of long history — each attestation is a signed, time-locked receipt for completed work. A Sybil attacker must pay the full cost of real work, separately, for every fake identity, while honest agents compound one history. Forging the receipts costs more than the work itself, so spawning a thousand islands buys nothing.
